title: Transforming Software Development with Generative AI: Empirical Insights on Collaboration and Workflow
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot are changing everyday work practices and collaboration in software development. The authors focus on how GenAI affects productivity, learning, communication, and team dynamics, arguing that while these tools can accelerate routine work and support individual problem-solving, they may also reduce human-to-human knowledge sharing.

The study is an exploratory multi-case qualitative interview study conducted across companies that had introduced GenAI into product development. The authors interviewed 13 adult professionals, including data scientists, managers, developers, designers, and frontend developers, about how they use GenAI and how it affects their workday. Reported uses included getting unstuck, learning new topics, creating virtual environments, copywriting, boilerplate generation, and working with existing code.

The paper concludes that GenAI increases perceived efficiency, motivation, and enjoyment, but can also disrupt established teamwork and learning loops by shifting interactions away from colleagues toward the AI tool. It also identifies practical concerns around confidentiality, anonymization, tool integration, prompt engineering skill, and the need to carefully contextualize outputs for local team practices. Overall, the paper frames GenAI as a useful but double-edged addition to software teams rather than a fully reliable replacement for peer collaboration.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on GPT-family large language models, used for conversational assistance, text and code generation, and interactive prompting.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by software professionals for assistance when stuck, learning, copywriting, boilerplating code/text, working with existing code, and prompt-engineered interactions; also used in simulated/virtual environment creation.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative interview study with 13 software professionals, participants reported that ChatGPT helped them get unstuck, work more efficiently, and reduce time spent on repetitive or menial tasks. It was described as faster than asking colleagues or searching Google, but the paper reports perceptions rather than quantified effects.
findings.measure: Interview-reported productivity, speed, and ease of use

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported that ChatGPT supported interactive learning, acted like a 'personal tutor,' and helped them learn new topics faster. The paper also notes that prompt engineering and role-based prompting improved precision and quality of responses.

The paper reports that using ChatGPT reduced some human-to-human interaction and pair programming, disrupting the team's learning loop and knowledge sharing. It also notes concerns about data confidentiality, anonymization of input, cultural bias in outputs, and the need to align prompts with agile context, but these are reported as perceived challenges rather than measured outcomes.
findings.measure: Interview-reported collaboration, knowledge sharing, and workflow disruption

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative multi-case interview study with 13 participants, so it provides useful practice-based evidence but not experimental causal estimates. The paper reports perceptions and themes rather than measured intervention effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported benefits are meaningful but unquantified, and the paper does not provide effect sizes. Because the evidence is qualitative and centered on workflow perceptions rather than measured impact, the overall impact tier is unclear/modest.
